whitelist_policy.note: A whitelist target is either a leaf service or the shared-state module. Every entry of module_import_whitelist.files must be registered below with a date and evidence (lint rule F5), so the whitelist cannot grow silently: widening it is a reviewable one-line data diff that carries its own justification.

leaf_service_criteria.L1: no reverse dependency: the module imports no domain module, no other leaf service and never ../app.js (only frontend/modules/utils/ and frontend/shared/). Enforced mechanically by F5.
leaf_service_criteria.L2: no domain semantics: its behaviour does not branch on domain state (it never asks 'batch or single task?' to decide what to do).
leaf_service_criteria.L3: no domain-owned state: it owns at most its own presentation state (throttle queue, last message) and owns no domain object (task, queue item, preview).

whitelist_policy.when_a_service_stops_qualifying: If a registered leaf service ever needs domain state or domain branching, it stops being a leaf service: drop it from the whitelist and inject it from app.js instead. Do not relax L1-L3.

frontend/modules/api-state.js.evidence: The single mutable value that the api-base domain (D1) owns and the pipeline (D8) reads (3 sites, :1787-1789). Design rev3 section 4.1 (option B): extracted by mutability from api-config.js. It is re-written after boot - by the 12s KIE-cold retry inside applyHealthToFooter and by startProcessing's own applyHealthToFooter call - so a 'pass it once' injection would go stale; the live binding keeps D8's 3 reads byte-identical. Imports nothing (L1 holds); holds an API-layer response cache, not a domain object such as task / queue-item / preview, so L3 holds.

frontend/modules/preview-state.js.evidence: Not a leaf service by design: it is the explicit live-binding channel for cross-domain reads. B1a moved the 6 preview slots here, plus the two pipeline-owned (D8) values other domains read - lastRenderedAnalysisResult (D10 :2918-2919, D9) and lastFetchedBlocks (D9 :4208, found only after the state-read scan was fixed to stop skipping declaration lines). 23 assignment sites became setter calls, every read expression stayed byte-identical, and all URL.revokeObjectURL calls stayed at their original call sites so statement order is unchanged. L1 also applies (this module imports nothing), so it cannot become a hub either.

frontend/modules/notifications.js.callers: 65 call sites / 8 domains (D14 17, D8 16, D4 11, D3 8, D10 4, D15 4, D5 3, D6 2)
frontend/modules/notifications.js.evidence: Touches only DOM (icon, colour, auto-dismiss); imports nothing but itself; owns no domain state; the same (message, type) always renders the same notification, regardless of who called it or when. Whitelisting it keeps all 65 call sites byte-identical, which is what makes the B1 'behaviour unchanged' claim provable.

frontend/modules/status-bar.js.evidence: Touches only DOM; owns only presentation state (statusUpdateQueue, isProcessingQueue, lastStatusMessage, STATUS_UPDATE_MIN_INTERVAL) and no other domain reads it (state_owners D2 is read cross-domain: never); every caller gets the same throttled rendering behaviour. Needed in B1 because D1 api-base is extracted in that batch and calls updateStatusBar 4 times. lastStatusUpdateTime was written but never read and was removed in the P-010 cleanup (2026-09-17).

frontend/modules/kie-config.js.evidence: Five immutable constants (const in app.js :1462-1466, never reassigned - measured 2026-09-15) moved verbatim; imports nothing at all and owns no mutable state, so no setter channel is needed. Needed because the options dialog (D6) and kie-mapping (D7) both read them and F3 forbids domain-to-domain imports: without this, the batch that moves the options dialog would have hit an unavoidable D6 -> D7 import. The dependency only became visible after the state-read scan stopped skipping declaration lines.

frontend/modules/api-config.js.callers: constant reads: D11 :3520, D12 :3674, D15 :5365 (B1) plus D10/D4/D8 in later batches; written once at load for api-base
frontend/modules/api-config.js.evidence: Four immutable values (API_BASE_URL / API_ROOT_URL / HEALTH_URL / ENGINES_URL) plus the two URL helpers that build them (moved verbatim from app.js :33-55/:57-64). Measured 2026-09-15: all four were const and are never reassigned after load, so they need no setter. The helpers did NOT go to modules/utils/ because the C6 gate asserts zero document/window refs there and resolveApiBaseUrl has 7 (window.location / window.DOCUVISION_CONFIG); keeping them here also means this module imports nothing at all, so L1 holds trivially. Splitting the config out of api-base.js is what lets every consumer import it while api-base itself stays unregistered - api-base calls status-bar, which would conflict with L1.
